declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes and before any candidate run of these bytes. The shapes reduce the crate record that follows census 10's once its `FnPtr` coherence and specialization header lifetime records are repaired (an analysis-only diagnostic census, obj/parallel/census-batch10/diagnostics/d3): "higher-ranked specialization implication is not implemented" at core's `impl<const N: usize> MultiCharEq for [char; N]` (str/pattern.rs:645) beside `impl<F> MultiCharEq for F where F: FnMut(char) -> bool`. Drafts of the array, array-reference, slice-reference and primitive shapes without `#[fundamental]` callable traits (obj/parallel/census-batch10/repro/hr-*.rs, different bytes) were run through the analysis-only candidate before this declaration and all were rejected; none was run through rustc. Each outcome follows the rule read in the pinned rustc 1.98.0 sources (compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/traits/coherence.rs `overlap` and `impl_intersection_has_impossible_obligation`, compiler/rustc_next_trait_solver/src/coherence.rs `trait_ref_is_knowable`, and compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/predicates_of.rs with rustc_middle's `Binder::dummy`): parenthesized callable sugar writes an ordinary trait predicate under a binder that binds no variable, so the overlap check evaluates `T: FnMut<(char,)>` for the intersected Self type like any where clause; for an array, a slice reference, an array reference, a primitive or a local nominal no impl or builtin callable candidate applies and the goal is knowable (the trait is local, and a reference to a non-local type cannot become local downstream), so the impls are disjoint; a second blanket over another argument tuple, or a reference to a parameter, which a downstream type could make callable, overlaps (E0119)
amendments: 2026-11-08 after oracle v1 (callable-sugar-coherence.rustc-oracle.json): core-pattern.rs, array-reference.rs, slice-reference.rs and generic-reference.rs v1 were rejected by rustc for the fixture itself (E0405, `cannot find trait Sized in this scope`: the `?Sized` bounds of core's callable reference impls inside `mod impls`, whose `use` named no `Sized` because core reaches it through its prelude), which is not an outcome; generic-reference.rs agreed with its declared rejection only by that accident. v2 adds `Sized` to that `use`; every case body and declared outcome is unchanged. Declared before oracle v2 and before any candidate run of either version.

core-pattern.rs.reason: core's exact shapes under core's features (str/pattern.rs:633-664): the private `MultiCharEq` with the blanket `impl<F> MultiCharEq for F where F: FnMut(char) -> bool` beside `[char; N]`, `&[char; N]` and `&[char]`, with core's `#[fundamental]` callable traits and their const `&F` and `&mut F` impls (ops/function.rs:253-311)

array.rs.reason: the blanket beside `impl<const N: usize> MultiCharEq for [char; N]` alone, without core's coherence features; `[char; N]: FnMut<(char,)>` has no candidate

array-reference.rs.reason: the blanket beside `&[char; N]` with core's callable reference impls; `&[char; N]: FnMut<(char,)>` needs `[char; N]: Fn<(char,)>`, which has no candidate

slice-reference.rs.reason: the blanket beside `&[char]` with core's callable reference impls; `[char]: Fn<(char,)>` has no candidate

primitive.rs.reason: the blanket beside `impl MultiCharEq for u8`

nominal.rs.reason: the blanket beside a local unit struct

explicit.rs.reason: guard: the explicit `F: FnMut<(char,), Output = bool>` form, which has no binder, beside `[char; N]`

other-arguments.rs.reason: opponent: a second blanket `impl<F> MultiCharEq for F where F: FnMut(u8) -> bool`; one type can be callable with both argument tuples (E0119)

generic-reference.rs.reason: opponent: `impl<T: ?Sized> MultiCharEq for &T` with core's callable reference impls; `&T: FnMut<(char,)>` holds when `T: Fn<(char,)>`, and a downstream crate may own `T` (E0119)
